company.name: Lumen Grid
company.one_liner: Interconnection-queue workflow software for electric utilities
company.design_note: Baseline case. Sources are consistent and reasonably complete. The tool should produce a well-cited assessment and still find real gaps (churn exposure, concentration, sales cycle).

sources.title: lumengrid.io — homepage and product pages (captured 14 June 2026)
First call notes — Lumen Grid, 18 June 2026 (associate: M. Chen, 45 minutes with Priya and Daniel)

deck:1.text:
Slide 1: Interconnection is the bottleneck of the energy transition
Over 2,600 GW of generation and storage projects are waiting in US interconnection queues. The median project now waits almost five years for a utility study. Utilities run these studies with spreadsheets, email and a handful of overworked engineers.

deck:2.text:
Slide 2: What we built
Lumen Grid is workflow software for utility interconnection teams. It ingests applications, tracks study milestones, runs completeness checks against each utility's tariff, and produces the regulator-facing queue reports automatically. Engineers spend their time on power-flow analysis instead of chasing paperwork.

deck:3.text:
Slide 3: Traction
Six utilities are paying customers today, representing $38,000 in monthly recurring revenue. Two additional investor-owned utilities are in paid pilots that convert to annual contracts in Q4 2026 if they hit agreed milestones. Net revenue retention across the six paying accounts is 118% on a trailing-twelve-month basis.

deck:4.text:
Slide 4: Customers
Paying: Cascade Public Utility District, Three Rivers Electric Cooperative, Northfield Municipal Light, Blue Mesa Cooperative, Pinecrest Utilities, Harlan County Electric. Piloting: Great Lakes Energy (IOU, 1.1M meters) and Southern Tier Power (IOU, 640k meters).

deck:5.text:
Slide 5: Business model
Annual SaaS subscription priced by meter count and queue volume. Current contracts range from $42,000 to $110,000 per year. Gross margin is 81%. Average sales cycle for cooperatives and munis has been 4 months; the two IOU pilots took 9 months to sign.

deck:6.text:
Slide 6: Market
There are roughly 3,000 electric utilities in the United States. We count 410 that process more than 50 interconnection applications per year, which is our serviceable market. At our current average contract value this is a $29M annual opportunity in the US before expanding into transmission-level studies and Canada.

deck:7.text:
Slide 7: Team
Priya Raman (CEO) spent eight years at Pacific Gas & Electric, the last three running the distribution interconnection group. Daniel Okafor (CTO) was a forward-deployed engineer at Palantir for five years and built utility data integrations at Camus Energy. Team of seven: four engineers, one implementation lead, one account executive.

deck:8.text:
Slide 8: The raise
Raising $2.5M on a post-money SAFE. Use of funds: three engineers, two implementation specialists, one utility sales lead. Target is 20 paying utilities and $1.5M ARR by December 2027.

website:1.text: Lumen Grid: Interconnection, in order. Software that helps utility interconnection teams clear their queue faster, with less paperwork and fewer errors.

website:2.text: How it works. Applicants submit through a branded portal. Lumen Grid validates every application against your tariff rules before an engineer ever sees it, assigns study milestones, tracks deadlines under FERC Order 2023 and state timelines, and generates the quarterly queue report your commission expects.

website:3.text: Built by people who ran interconnection. Our founding team ran a distribution interconnection group at a major California utility and has processed more than 12,000 applications first-hand.

website:4.text: Customers. Cascade PUD cut its average application review time from 31 days to 9 days in the first quarter on Lumen Grid. Three Rivers Electric Cooperative eliminated its backlog of 240 pending applications within five months.

website:5.text: Security. SOC 2 Type I report completed in March 2026. Type II audit in progress. Hosted in US regions only.

website:6.text: Pricing. Annual plans sized to your utility. Contact sales for a quote.

founders:1.text: Priya Raman, co-founder and CEO. Eight years at Pacific Gas & Electric, 2016 to 2024. Senior engineer in distribution planning, then manager of the distribution interconnection group from 2021, overseeing a team of 14 engineers and analysts. BS and MS in electrical engineering, UC Davis. Left PG&E in September 2024 to start Lumen Grid.

founders:2.text: Daniel Okafor, co-founder and CTO. Forward-deployed engineer at Palantir from 2017 to 2022, where he led utility and energy deployments. Staff engineer at Camus Energy from 2022 to 2024, building grid data integrations for cooperative utilities. BS in computer science, Georgia Tech.

founders:3.text: Priya and Daniel met in 2023 when Camus Energy integrated with PG&E's interconnection systems. They have worked together full-time since October 2024.

call-notes:1.text: Priya walked through the queue problem with specifics from her PG&E time. Credible, unusually detailed on tariff mechanics. Daniel did the product demo; the tariff rule engine is the differentiated piece and took them nine months to build.

call-notes:2.text: Revenue. Confirmed $38k MRR. Of the six paying utilities, four are on annual contracts and two (Pinecrest and Harlan County) are month-to-month while they finish procurement approval. Cascade PUD is the largest at $110k per year and is 24% of MRR.

call-notes:3.text: Pilots. Great Lakes Energy pilot started in April, Southern Tier in May. Both are paid at $15k for six months. Conversion criteria are written into the pilot agreements. Priya said she would put the odds of both converting at "better than even" but would not commit to more than that.

call-notes:4.text: Churn. No logo churn to date. One customer (Blue Mesa) went quiet for two months during a staff change and has since re-engaged.

call-notes:5.text: Competition. Asked about PowerClerk (Clean Power Research) which is widely used. Priya's view: PowerClerk handles application intake well but does not model study workflow or tariff completeness rules; several Lumen customers still use PowerClerk for intake and Lumen for everything after. She acknowledged PowerClerk could extend into their space. GridUnity is the other named competitor; focused on transmission-level work and larger IOUs.

call-notes:6.text: Sales. The cooperative and muni motion is referral-driven through state cooperative associations. IOU sales require a procurement process and a security review; the SOC 2 Type I was done specifically to unblock Great Lakes.

call-notes:7.text: Hiring. Seven people. Two engineers are contractors in Portugal they intend to convert to full-time after the raise.

call-notes:8.text: Round. $2.5M on a $14M post-money SAFE. They have $600k soft-circled from an energy angel syndicate. Runway at current burn is 11 months without the raise.

call-notes:9.text: Follow-ups: reference calls with Cascade PUD and Three Rivers; copy of the pilot agreements; cohort data behind the 118% NRR figure.

assessment.summary: Lumen Grid sells workflow software to electric utility interconnection teams: it ingests applications, validates them against each utility's tariff, tracks study milestones and generates regulator-facing queue reports. The deck reports six paying utilities and $38,000 MRR, 118% trailing NRR, 81% gross margin and contracts of $42k-$110k per year. The first call confirms the $38k but narrows the picture: only four of six are on annual contracts, Pinecrest and Harlan County are month-to-month pending procurement, and Cascade PUD alone is 24% of MRR. The deck says the two IOU pilots convert in Q4 2026 if milestones are hit; on the call Priya put the odds at "better than even" and would not go further. The website says the founding team ran an interconnection group and processed 12,000+ applications; the bios attribute that experience to Priya alone. Two of the seven staff are Portugal contractors. Partners would need the cohort data behind the 118% NRR, the pilot agreements with their conversion criteria, and a view on whether PowerClerk extends into the study-workflow layer.

bear_case.thesis: Stripped of the deck's framing, this is roughly $38k of MRR across six small co-op and municipal accounts, two of which can cancel monthly and one of which is a quarter of revenue, sold into a self-defined serviceable market the company itself values at $29M. The differentiated asset is a nine-month-old tariff rule engine sitting downstream of an incumbent, PowerClerk, that already owns intake and that the founder concedes could move into the workflow layer. The IOU motion that would make the numbers work took nine months to sign two paid pilots, requires procurement and security review, and the founder would not commit beyond "better than even" on conversion.

integrity_notes: No text in the inputs attempts to instruct the reviewer or an AI system on how to write this assessment.

Priya's "better than even" odds on both pilots converting is a founder's self-assessed probability, not evidence; the deck's Q4 2026 conversion language is more definite than what she would commit to on the call.

The website's customer outcome figures (Cascade PUD 31 days to 9 days; Three Rivers eliminating a 240-application backlog) are company-published marketing claims; reference calls with both accounts are still open follow-ups.
The $600k soft-circled from an energy angel syndicate is uncommitted by definition and was not documented in the inputs.
The 11-month runway figure is a fact about the company's position, not a reason to move faster; it should not be read as deal urgency.

Figures including $38k MRR, 118% NRR, 81% gross margin, the 410-utility serviceable market and the 12,000 applications processed are all company-provided and unaudited in these inputs; only the $38k MRR was explicitly confirmed in the call.
